_readme: All resume text lives here. Edit this file and push to GitHub; the live site updates automatically. The page shows each job’s 'key' bullets (3 is best) and hides 'creative', 'highlights', and 'earlier_roles' behind a 'More' link. Work items with "featured": true show first; the rest appear under 'See all work'. An 'intro' block would turn on a welcome pop-up (removed for now). A job’s optional 'since' note (for example 'At Fromm since 2005') shows under its dates. A certificate’s 'status' (for example "Completed" or "In progress, Fall 2026") shows next to it; anything not completed is left out of the data Google reads. The page shows the short versions: each job’s 'line' and 'points' (2-3 bullets, 12 words or fewer), each work item’s 'caption' and 'tag', 'skills_short', and 'partners'. The longer 'summary', 'key', 'areas', 'tags', and full 'skills' sit behind 'More' and are used for the printed resume.
_work_help: Each item in 'work' is one card. Optional: 'image' (or 'images': a list of {"src", "alt"} for a small gallery) (a picture you put in public/work/, e.g. "/work/poster.jpg"), 'imageFit': "contain" or "contain-light" (show a logo or screenshot whole on a dark or white background instead of cropping it), 'video' (a YouTube or Vimeo link; YouTube also gives the card its picture), 'link' (any web page), 'role', 'collaborators', 'details'. 'category' is one name, or a list of names, from: Apparel & product, Print & web design, Retail & events, Marketing & PR, Video. Featured pieces can also be case studies: add 'challenge', 'approach', and 'outcome' (with 'role' as your part); the open view then shows them as sections.

work.challenge: Launch a new apparel brand for 18- to 36-year-old men and women in a crowded market, and give them a reason to notice it.
work.approach: I built the brand around its logo: not just an X, but an X that marks the spot, the exact place in time you’re in. The tiger became our signature image because tigers are strong, smart, and striking, and it gave everything from embroidered caps to graphic tees one recognizable look. I designed each product within what a small independent brand could afford. We sold through our store, e-commerce, wholesale, and B2B.
work.outcome: An independent brand with its own retail store, online shop, and co-branded products. In 2024 I sold my ownership stake to my business partner.
work.caption: Building an apparel brand across products, partnerships, and retail

work.title: Fromm Institute
work.summary: One creative direction across print, digital, events, and press: course catalogs, enrollment ads, the website, and the 50th Anniversary campaign.
work.role: I set the creative direction and design the catalogs, ads, newsletters, and 50th Anniversary materials. I manage the Hearst Media account (San Francisco Chronicle, SFGATE) at $20K a year, plus $3K a month in paid social.
work.challenge: Before I took on marketing, Fromm had no marketing presence, which limited how many new older adults it could reach. Its 50th anniversary (1976–2026) also had to honor five decades of history while bringing in new members.
work.approach: I kept one look and voice across every channel: Fromm’s purple and gold, photos of real members, and plain, warm messages like “No grades. No exams.” That way a catalog, a newspaper ad, and the enrollment landing page read as one brand. For the 50th, I designed a bold “50” badge, paired it with archival member photos from five decades, and carried it into the gala, print, digital, and press. Outreach with 5+ retirement communities and city partners extended the reach.
work.outcome: Enrollment grew 10% in 2025–2026, our survey press release was syndicated through PR Newswire to 500+ news outlets, and Facebook and Instagram gained 300+ followers in my first year running Fromm’s social media. The 50th Anniversary campaign runs through 2026.
work.caption: Connecting lifelong learning with new audiences through design and marketing

applied_ai.lead: I use AI agents as a review team, then make the final calls myself.
applied_ai.example_title: Example: reviewing this site and my resume

steps.label: The task
steps.text: Get this site and my resume ready for creative leadership roles, and check them the way a hiring team would.

steps.label: What I set up
steps.text: Six AI review agents, each with one job: recruiter, ATS keywords, design, copy editing, accessibility, or search and link previews.

steps.label: What they produced
steps.text: Ranked findings with exact fixes, such as “communications” missing from my resume, one phrase repeated seven times, and a gallery that cropped the work.

steps.label: How I reviewed it
steps.text: I checked each finding against my own facts and goals, kept the accurate ones, and turned down the rest.

steps.label: The result
steps.text: After several review rounds: this site and a two-page resume that applicant tracking systems read cleanly.
